full_text:
India's eastern coastline is facing a significant weather threat as Cyclone Murasu continues moving towards Andhra Pradesh after strengthening into a severe cyclonic storm.
According to the latest available India Meteorological Department coastal weather bulletin, issued at 9:22 AM IST on November 2, the storm was centred over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal near latitude 13.9°N and longitude 81.8°E.
Editorial Insight
Key Highlights
Important points readers should notice.
Issue/Event: Cyclone Murasu has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal.
Location: India.
Authority/Organisation: India Meteorological Department (IMD).
Action Taken: Severe cyclone warnings issued, with Great Danger signals raised at several coastal ports.
Impact: Strong winds, heavy rainfall, rough seas and potential storm-surge inundation threaten coastal communities.
The system was approximately 200 kilometres east-northeast of Chennai, 210 kilometres east-southeast of Nellore and 260 kilometres southeast of Ongole.
The IMD expects the cyclone to move northwestwards and cross the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur, close to Ongole. The anticipated landfall window is between 11:30 PM on November 2 and 4:00 AM on November 3.
At the time of landfall, sustained wind speeds are expected to reach 100–110 kmph, with gusts of up to 120 kmph.
Editorial Analysis
Why This Matters
Cyclone Murasu presents significant risks to coastal communities and economic activities across southern Andhra Pradesh. The anticipated wind speeds could damage vulnerable houses, electricity infrastructure, roads and agricultural plantations. The projected storm surge is another major concern because seawater entering low-lying coastal areas can threaten homes, farmland and essential infrastructure. Fishing communities are particularly vulnerable because rough seas and strong winds can make maritime activities extremely dangerous. Timely weather information and adherence to official warnings will therefore be essential in reducing potential damage and protecting lives.
The weather system is also expected to produce widespread rainfall and deteriorating sea conditions along the affected coastline.
The IMD has warned that a storm surge of approximately 1.0–1.5 metres above the astronomical tide could inundate low-lying areas of south coastal Andhra Pradesh during landfall.
Bapatla, Krishna and Prakasam districts have been identified as areas where the maximum peak surge is expected.
The coastal weather bulletin also reported the replacement of local cautionary signals with Great Danger signals at several ports, including Krishnapatnam, Machilipatnam, Nizampatnam and Vadarevu.
Residents, fishermen and coastal communities have been advised to follow official weather warnings and local administration instructions.
